sections.html:
Frederick is Virginia's northernmost county. Winchester, the county seat, is an independent city that the county surrounds, so a Winchester mailing address does not automatically mean a Winchester tax bill. Check the bill's letterhead before you phone anyone.

Head counts: 91,419 residents in 2020, rising to an estimated 99,955 by 2025. The housing stock was 35,827 units in 2020, and owners occupied 78.8% of the homes that had someone living in them. Stephens City and Middletown are the incorporated towns. Plenty of sellers live outside both, in communities like Kernstown, Clear Brook, Round Hill, Jordan Springs, Lake Frederick and Mountain Falls, and Interstates 81 and 66 carry most commuter traffic.

The county posts $0.53 per $100 of assessed value for real estate, and mobile homes land on the identical figure. A real estate calculator is linked from the county's rate page, so you can enter your own assessment and see roughly what a year costs before you put a sign in the yard.

TaxRate
Real estate$0.53 per $100 of assessed value
Personal property$4.35 per $100
County meals tax6.0%

The Commissioner of the Revenue decides what your property is worth on paper. Billing and collection belong to the Treasurer. Take value disputes to the first office and payment questions to the second.

The year is paid in two installments, due June 5 and December 5. A due date that falls when the office is shut rolls to the next business day. Frederick's Treasurer, C. William Orndoff, Jr., also lets owners pre-pay real estate tax, which helps when you want a zero balance in hand ahead of a settlement.

  • January 1 to April 1: elderly and permanently disabled tax relief applications, due April 1.
  • June 5: opening installment for real estate and personal property.
  • November 1: land use applications, with a late filing fee accepted through December 1.
  • December 5: closing installment.

Late charges vary with how long a balance sits, so ask the Treasurer for today's penalty and interest before you trust any payoff total.

Call the assessor first, at 540-665-5680. Appeals are open to an owner who believes the Commissioner made a mistake, or that someone else made a factual error during a general reassessment. Gather recent nearby sale prices, photos of defects and any contractor quotes before you dial.

  1. An assessor hearing at the County Administration Building, 107 North Kent Street, Winchester. Book it at 540-722-8319 between 9 a.m. and 4 p.m. on weekdays. The Winchester Star and the county website carry hearing dates.
  2. A written appeal sent by email, by letter, or on the Appeal of Assessment form, addressed to Commissioner of the Revenue, Real Property Tax Appeal, PO Box 552, Winchester, VA 22604.
  3. If you are still unhappy, take it up with the Board of Equalization, and finally Frederick County Circuit Court.

Ask the office when the next reassessment cycle opens, since that sets your Board of Equalization window. Virginia Code 58.1-3984 governs court timing and treats the assessor's number as correct for real property until you prove otherwise.

Farm, horticulture and forestry parcels can qualify for reduced land use assessments through the Commissioner's Real Estate Division. Relief programs run through the same division: one for elderly and disabled owners, one for owners with a service-connected disability, and one for surviving spouses of certain people killed on duty. Owners rated totally and permanently disabled from service, and surviving spouses of armed forces members killed in action, may file whenever they like instead of meeting the spring cutoff.

If part of your acreage is in a use program, learn what happens to the deferral at sale before you pick a closing date. The division's page links the program rules and a Tax Sale Information Center.

Under Virginia Code 58.1-3340, tax left unpaid on a house becomes a lien that sits ahead of other claims and survives until somebody actually pays it. Money from a sale goes first toward taxes and levies on the property, and penalties and interest are folded into the tax itself. The settlement agent will find any balance and deduct it from what you receive. Your sales contract decides how the current year's tax is shared with the buyer.

Recording the deed adds a separate cost. Virginia Code 58.1-802 sets the grantor's tax at 50 cents for each $500 of consideration. The seller pays it unless the buyer takes it over by agreement.

sections.h2: What to bring to the office
sections.html:
Most Frederick County tax questions resolve faster with paper in hand. For the Commissioner of the Revenue, carry your parcel or account number, a copy of the latest assessment notice, and anything that shows why the figure is off: comparable sale prices, an inspection report, photos of damage. For the Treasurer, bring the account number and a copy of the settlement statement if a closing is already scheduled.

Appeals by mail should include the completed Appeal of Assessment form and the same supporting papers, sent to the PO Box 552 address in Winchester. Keep a copy of everything and note the date you mailed it. Hearings run by appointment only, so do not show up at North Kent Street on a whim.

Because the county splits the year at June 5 and December 5, a house that closes in the middle of the year usually has one half paid and one half pending. Sort out early who covers which stretch of ownership. If the first half is paid and you sell in the autumn, the buyer normally reimburses you for the months after the closing date, and you cover the rest of the December half. Your contract and the settlement statement spell out the split, so read them line by line.

Personal property tax is billed alongside real estate on the same June 5 schedule. A mobile home is taxed at the real estate rate rather than the higher personal property rate, which can surprise a seller who expected the larger figure. Ask the Commissioner how your own unit is classified.

Doing a few small errands early keeps the sale moving. Here is a sensible order.

  1. Phone the Treasurer for payoff numbers on both halves so you know whether anything is open.
  2. Request your current assessment from the Commissioner of the Revenue and set it beside recent sales on your street. If it looks high, weigh whether a hearing is worth your time before you choose an asking price.
  3. If you get elderly or disabled relief, or your land sits in a use program, ask what changes after a transfer and whether any back tax comes due.
  4. Confirm whether Winchester or the county bills you.
  5. Hand your closing agent the tax account numbers early so the proration and payoff are drafted well before the settlement date.

A cash purchase skips a lender's appraisal and underwriting. That shortens the calendar and leaves less room for a late-surfacing tax balance to delay things. The balance still comes out of your proceeds, because the lien rules apply to every kind of buyer.

faqs.q: What is the Frederick County real estate tax rate?
faqs.a: The rate is $0.53 per $100 of assessed value, and mobile homes are taxed at the same figure.

faqs.q: When are Frederick County real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: June 5 for the first half and December 5 for the second half. If the office is closed on a due date, the next business day applies.

faqs.q: Who do I call to dispute a Frederick County assessment?
faqs.a: Call the assessor at 540-665-5680. To schedule a hearing, call 540-722-8319 between 9 a.m. and 4 p.m. on weekdays.

faqs.q: Is Winchester part of Frederick County?
faqs.a: No. Winchester is the county seat but an independent city under Virginia law, and Frederick County surrounds it.

faqs.q: When is the Frederick County tax relief deadline for seniors?
faqs.a: Applications for elderly or permanently disabled relief are accepted from January 1 to April 1.
